Compute frame angular velocity from rotation matrices

Source: R/compute_frame_velocity.R
compute_frame_angular_velocity.Rd

Computes angular velocity from a time series of rotation matrices using finite differences. Central differences are used for interior frames, and either first- or second-order schemes are used at the endpoints.

Usage

compute_frame_angular_velocity(
  frame_array,
  dt,
  endpoints = c("first", "second"),
  enforce_skew = TRUE
)

Arguments

frame_array

A 3 x 3 x N numeric array of rotation matrices. Each slice frame_array[,,i] must be a valid rotation matrix representing the orientation of the segment in the global frame.

dt

Numeric scalar. Time step between frames (seconds).

endpoints

Character string specifying endpoint method:

"first"

First-order forward/backward difference (default)

"second"

Second-order forward/backward difference

enforce_skew

Logical. If TRUE, forces the angular velocity matrix to be skew-symmetric before extracting the vector. Recommended when working with noisy data.

Value

A list with:

  • frame_velocity3 x 3 x N array of angular velocity matrices

  • omegaN x 3 matrix of angular velocity vectors (global frame)

Details

Angular velocity is computed as: $$\Omega = \dot{R} R^T$$ where \(R\) is the rotation matrix. The angular velocity vector is extracted from the skew-symmetric matrix \(\Omega\).

All inputs and outputs are expressed in the global (inertial) frame.
